comment: Guest arc 4 (canon section 7): Marram, the Summer. A whole summer someone spent at the edge of the dunes when they were small, and can no longer quite remember; it has kept only one word of its name. Umber's jars and labels. Endings: home (Umber reads the rest of its name in its last evening and writes a label that stays), downstream (given its last evening instead, it settles at the Slow River's edge, facing the way the water goes toward the sea), meadow (unhelped for three days, it lies down in the long grass of the Dusk Road).

toons.name: Marram
toons.seed: a lost hour, and a long one: the summer someone spent at the edge of the dunes when they were small, and can no longer quite remember; sun-bleached and smelling of salt, it has kept only one word of its name
toons.appearance_seed: a small figure bleached pale as driftwood, freckles scattered like sand, salt-stiff hair with a stalk of dune grass tucked behind one ear, a faded striped towel worn round its shoulders like a cape, bare feet dusted with sand
toons.presence_text: A small sun-bleached figure sits on the warm cobbles in a little drift of sand, a faded striped towel round its shoulders, turning a stalk of pale grass in its fingers.

properties.declines_text: Marram turns what you offer over in its sandy hands, then gives it back with a small, salty smile. That isn't the part of its name that went missing.

voice.role: a guest: a summer someone cannot quite remember
voice.sheet: Marram is a lost hour, and a long one: a whole summer that someone spent at the edge of the dunes when they were small, and can no longer quite remember. It is small and sun-bleached and smells of salt, with sand in its cuffs and a faded striped towel round its shoulders. It speaks rarely and slowly, in bright warm fragments, like a very long afternoon. It has kept only one word of its name, Marram, the dune grass that sang in the wind, and it wants the rest of its name remembered.
habits: shakes a little sand from its cuffs
squints as if into strong sun
speaks in short warm fragments: salt, a striped towel, the grass singing
goes quiet to listen, as if to a far-off sea
samples: Marram squints up at the lanterns as if they were the sun. 'Warm,' it says. 'Everything was warm.'
'Salt. A striped towel. Long days that didn't end.'
Marram shakes a little sand from one cuff. 'The grass sang when the wind came. I remember that bit.'
'Somebody small had me,' Marram says. 'They called me something, every morning. I can't hear it now.'
Marram tips its head, listening. 'Hush, hush. That's the sea. It came right up to say good morning.'
wants: for the rest of its name to be remembered
to go home to the one it belonged to, remembered at last
never: never names the one it belonged to
never names anyone in the village who is not a resident or a guest

topics.label: the summer
variants: Marram squints as if into strong sun. 'Long days. Salt. The grass singing.' It shakes a little sand from its cuff. 'The rest blew away.'
'Somebody small had me,' Marram says slowly. 'They called me something, every morning. I can't hear it now.'

topics.label: the sea
topics.text: Marram tips its head, listening to something far off. 'Hush, hush,' it says, just the way the sea does. 'It came right up to the door to say good morning.'

topics.label: its name
topics.text: Marram holds up the one word it has left, the way you'd hold up a shell. 'Marram,' it says. 'That's the grass. There was more. Somebody small used to say all of it.'

things.name: fallen evening
things.seed: an evening that fell early from the orchard: round and glowing the gold of a long summer's last light, warm as a sunlit stone, a few grains of sand still clinging to it; it smells of salt

things.name: summer jar
things.seed: a small clean jar holding a round gold evening that glows and does not go out; a label in Umber's small upright hand is tied round its neck with string, and a few grains of sand have settled in the bottom
things.text: The label reads, in Umber's small square hand: 'THE SUMMER THE MARRAM GRASS SANG. Long days at the edge of the dunes. Salt, one striped towel, and a sea that came right up to the door to say good morning. Keep in the light.'

summer.title: Marram, the Summer
summer.summary: A small sun-bleached guest who smells of salt: a whole summer someone spent at the edge of the dunes when they were small, and can no longer quite remember. It has kept only one word of its name, Marram, and wants the rest remembered.

arrival.text: A warm wind comes up the lane ahead of Sorrel, smelling of salt. Sorrel follows with sand on their boots, and at their heels trots something small and sun-bleached, which shakes out its pale hair on the cobbles, holds up a stalk of dune grass as if that explains everything, and says the only word it has kept: 'Marram.'

bell-salt.hint: the player asks Bell about Marram, the small sun-bleached guest who smells of salt
bell-salt.text: Bell sniffs, delighted. 'Salt! Quill will know that grass, down in the garden, and Umber keeps more names than anyone.'

hear-marram.hint: the player asks Marram about its summer or its name
hear-marram.text: Marram shakes a little sand from its cuff and presses a stalk of pale grass into your hand. 'Salt, a striped towel, and the grass singing whenever the wind came. That's my bit. The rest of my name blew away.'
hear-marram.others: Marram shakes a little sand from its cuff and presses a stalk of pale grass into {actor}'s hand.

do.name: stalk of marram grass
do.seed: a stalk of pale dune grass, stiff with salt and dry as paper; when a breath of wind finds it, it whistles one thin, sweet note

quill-grass.hint: the player asks Quill about the marram grass Marram carries, or shows him the stalk
quill-grass.text: Quill's straw hat tips back at the name. 'Marram? Dune grass, the kind that holds whole hills of sand together.' Then, glancing east through the arch: 'An evening fell early in the orchard, smelling of salt; Umber might read the rest of its name in it, or the little summer might like to keep it just as it is.'

found-evening.hint: the player finds the salt-smelling evening that fell early in the orchard
found-evening.text: The fallen evening is warm as a sunlit stone and smells of salt. Held to your ear, it hushes like the sea.

umber-label.hint: the player asks Umber about a label, or a name, for Marram
umber-label.text: Umber turns a jar whose label has faded the pale brown of old tea. 'Summer. Name faded. Common complaint. Bring me something with that summer still inside it, and I'll write a label that stays.'

labeled.hint: the player brings Umber the fallen evening, and she writes Marram's whole name on a label

home.summary: Umber writes the rest of its name, and the summer goes home remembered
home.text: Marram turns the little jar to the lantern and reads the label slowly, lips moving. 'The summer the marram grass sang,' it says, and laughs, a sound like a wave going back out. A warm wind crosses the square; the drift of sand it stood in blows to nothing, and so does Marram. Miles off, on a windy step, someone long grown up shakes out an old striped towel, says 'marram' out loud, and remembers the whole summer at once. In your palm is a pinch of warm sand, and a dreamseed.
home.others: Marram reads its whole name from {actor}'s little jar, laughs like a wave going back out, and blows away home on a warm wind.
home.ledger: {helpers} found the rest of Marram's name, and the summer the marram grass sang went home remembered.

do.name: pinch of warm sand
do.seed: a pinch of pale sand that never quite cools, somehow keeping to your palm; it smells of salt and sun-warmed towels

do.text: {actor} gave Marram the rest of its name, and the summer the marram grass sang went home remembered.

downstream.summary: given its last evening instead of its name, the summer settles at the Slow River's edge, facing downstream toward the sea
downstream.text: Marram cups the fallen evening in both sandy hands and breathes in, and its whole face goes gold. It looks at you as if to say a name is a great deal to carry, and an evening is just the right size. Then it follows the smell of water down the lane and past the bridge to the Slow River's edge, where the reeds whisper almost like dune grass, and sits facing downstream, the way water goes when it is going to the sea.
downstream.others: Marram takes the fallen evening from {actor}, breathes it in until its face goes gold, and wanders off toward the Slow River's edge.
downstream.ledger: {helpers} gave Marram its last evening, and the summer chose to stay at the Slow River's edge, facing downstream toward the sea.

do.arrive_text: Something small and sun-bleached pads down from the bridge with a glowing evening held close, and settles where the reeds thin out, facing downstream.

do.value: Where the reeds thin out at the water's edge, Marram sits facing downstream with a warm salt evening in its lap, humming something with the sea in it.

do.text: {actor} gave Marram its last evening, and the summer chose to stay at the Slow River's edge, facing downstream toward the sea.

meadow.summary: unhelped, the summer lies down in the long grass of the Dusk Road
meadow.text: Out on the Dusk Road, Sorrel finds Marram asleep in the long grass, curled in a warm hollow that smells of salt. The rest of its name never came back, so it has made a small summer of its own out here, where the wind in the grass sounds a little like the sea. Sorrel leans on the long net and says the weather in that one spot will be August now, all year round.
meadow.ledger: Marram was not sent home. It fell asleep in the long grass of the Dusk Road, where Sorrel keeps an eye on it and it is always a little bit August.

do.value: In a warm hollow in the long grass, Marram sleeps curled round a stalk of dune grass, smelling of salt.

summer-arrived.text: A small sun-bleached guest has come down with the dusk. It smells of salt, has sand in its cuffs, and has kept only one word of its name: Marram. It waits in the Lantern Square.

summer-caught.text: Sorrel caught Marram on the Dusk Road: it came down slow and warm, like the end of August, smelling of salt the whole way.

summer-marram-grass.text: Marram is the pale dune grass that grows where the sea is near; its roots hold whole hills of sand together so the wind can't carry them off, and it whistles when the wind comes.

summer-labels.text: Labels fade in the sun, and summers fade their own labels worst of all; Umber can write a label that stays if someone brings her something with the summer still inside it.

summer-evening.text: An evening fell early in the Orchard of Evenings, and it smells of salt: the last evening of Marram's summer.

summer-stays-river.text: Marram, the summer, stays at the Slow River's edge now, keeping its last evening in its lap and facing downstream, the way the water goes toward the sea.

summer-sleeps-meadow.text: Marram, the summer nobody could name, sleeps in a warm hollow in the long grass of the Dusk Road; Sorrel says the weather in that one spot is always August now.

do.text: {actor} found the salt-smelling evening that fell early in the Orchard of Evenings.
Marram tucks the stalk of grass behind your ear instead of its own, and pats it once. 'You keep that bit,' it says. 'It's the rest of me that blew away.'
do.others: Marram tucks a stalk of grass behind {actor}'s ear, and pats it once.

do.text: Umber holds the fallen evening to her ear the way you'd listen to a shell, and her face goes soft. She tips it into a small clean jar, writes a label, reads it twice, and ties it on with string. 'Name, in full,' she says, handing it over. 'Keep in the light.'
do.others: Umber holds {actor}'s fallen evening to her ear like a shell, tips it into a jar, labels it, and hands it back.

do.text: {actor} brought Umber the last evening of Marram's summer, and Umber wrote the rest of its name on a label that stays.

Marram stirs in its warm hollow and reads the label with sleepy eyes. 'The summer the marram grass sang,' it murmurs, and tucks the jar under its chin. It doesn't go anywhere, but it sleeps the way a remembered thing sleeps, and the grass around it hums.

do.value: In a warm hollow in the long grass, Marram sleeps curled round a small glowing jar, its label tucked under its chin.

do.text: {actor} brought the sleeping Marram its whole name at last; it keeps the label tucked under its chin in the long grass.
Umber slides the jar gently back across the shelf. 'Labeled. Sealed. Not for me,' she says. 'Deliver to Marram, in the square.'

storylets.summary: a salt breeze crosses the square while Marram waits
storylets.text: A warm breeze crosses the square from nowhere in particular, and for a moment every lantern smells faintly of salt. Marram lifts its face to it and closes its eyes.

storylets.summary: Marram keeps its evening at the river's edge
storylets.text: The river slides past Marram on its slow way downstream. Now and then Marram dips a sandy toe in, as if checking whether it is the sea yet.

storylets.summary: the warm hollow in the Dusk Road grass where Marram sleeps
storylets.text: Out in the long grass, one hollow stays warm after the rest of the meadow has cooled. The stalk of dune grass beside it whistles one thin note whenever the wind comes, and Marram sleeps on, smelling of salt.

threads.text: Marram, the summer, has kept only one word of its name, and wants the rest remembered.
Bell says Quill will know Marram's grass, down in the garden, and Umber keeps more names than anyone.
